Tombstone , which Yang began working on when he retired from Xinhua in 1996, is the most authoritative account of the Great Famine.

...

From the government documents he consulted, Yang concluded that 36 million people died and 40 million children were not born as a result of the famine. Yang’s father was among the victims and Yang says this book is meant to be his tombstone.

...

But Yang has gone further, using his contacts around the country to penetrate closely guarded Communist Party archives and uncover more direct proof of the number of dead, the cases of cannibalism, and the continued systematic efforts of the state to cover up this colossal tragedy. This makes Tombstone one of the most important books to come out of China in recent years and led the government to ban it.
Ian Johnson : I wondered when reading Tombstone why officials didn’t destroy the files. Why did they preserve all this evidence?
